title: Gallery
text: This page first builds a chart by hand from plain curves, then shows a range of other charts, each with the code that draws it.

title: A chart built piece by piece
text: Every chart in this package is a set of Scales: curves that take a value to a point on the page. The constructions, such as additive_nomogram, work out those curves for you. title: Rendering
text: drawing turns a nomogram into a NomogramDrawing. This holds the axis polylines, tick positions, normals and labels, and isopleth segments: the geometry of the chart, with no information about how to draw it. text: The defaults follow the proportions of a standard d3 axis: hairline rules, short ticks and small type. Everything in NomogramStyle is measured in chart units. title: Ticks
text: Tick values are chosen to be round numbers in the variable, then thinned by their distance apart on the page (thin_ticks). Doing it in that order keeps a non-uniform axis readable. title: One curved scale
text: A formula with no chart on three straight scales may still have one on two straight scales and a curve. The classic example is the roots of a quadratic. auto_nomogram finds this chart from the formula for the root, so you do not have to derive a determinant. A line from p to q crosses the curve at …

title: More than two inputs
text: One alignment line relates only three scales, so a formula with three or more inputs becomes a chain of charts linked by unmarked pivot lines. You lay a line across the first stage, note where it crosses the pivot line, then pivot about that point to read the next stage. auto_nomogram finds the …

title: How the result is checked
text: If the inputs have units, auto_nomogram first checks the formula's dimensions. For example, if the result should be in kg/m² and the formula gives kg/m, the formula is refused before any chart is built. Once the chart is built, it is solved over a grid of inputs and every answer is compared with …

title: Four or more variables
text: One alignment line can relate only three scales. For more variables there are two approaches: chain charts together through a shared scale, or let one point carry two variables at once. auto_nomogram builds chains automatically for formulas that allow them. This page shows how to build either kind …

text: A relation of four variables in proportion, f₁(u) / f₂(v) = f₃(w) / f₄(t), needs no separate stages. proportional_nomogram draws two N charts on top of each other, sharing their diagonal. Each upright line carries two variables, labelled on opposite sides. Lay a line from u to v, then a …

title: Grids
text: A pivot line works only when the first two variables combine into a single intermediate value. When they do not, one of the three points on an alignment line has to carry two variables at once. That point lies on a Grid: a two-parameter surface (u, v) -> (x, y), drawn as a mesh. This is the grid …

title: Bibliography
text: Nomography dates from the nineteenth century and has a long textbook tradition. This page lists the works this documentation draws on, and where to read more.

title: The founding text
text: Maurice d'Ocagne. Traité de nomographie. Théorie des abaques, applications pratiques. Paris: Gauthier-Villars, 1899. A public-domain scan is on the Internet Archive.The alignment method, in which three points lie on one straight line and the condition is written as a vanishing determinant, is …

title: Textbooks
text: L. Ivan Epstein. Nomography. New York: Interscience, 1958.Edward Otto. Nomography. New York: Macmillan, 1963. text: A nomogram rests on a single condition: a point taken from each scale lies on one straight line exactly when the values satisfy the relation. text: Projective maps also keep collinear points collinear, and they are a much larger family than affine maps. text: DEFAULT_ISOPLETH_DASHES Dash patterns, cycled one step behind the colours, so a fourth isopleth is dashed blue instead of a second plain blue. Lines are never told apart by colour alone, so a chart can carry more lines than there are safe colours.
